My parents are divorced, and my mother is solely responsible for my 12-year-old brother and me (almost 18 years old). Our lives changed when my father took all the money from the joint bank account he shared with my mother, leaving her without any funds. Fortunately, my mother works full-time as a French teacher, allowing my brother and me to attend school for free. For the past four years, my father has been forced to send a court-mandated amount of 800,000 LL per month. To avoid contact with him and to protect us, my mother receives the payment through a lawyer, who takes 200,000 LL each month, and 50,000 LL is deducted for OMT transfer fees. We effectively receive 550,000 LL from him each month. My mother has no property other than half of our apartment, where we currently live. The only car we use belongs to my father. He hasn't taken it back because, according to the law, he would be obligated to cover our transportation costs while we are minors. He will probably reclaim it once my brother turns 18. Because I am determined, diligent, and responsible, I continue to hope to change my life by having a successful professional future. For me, AUB is the best university to achieve this. Throughout my schooling, I have consistently ranked among the top three in my class, and I do not want to give up. I still believe in life's justice to give me the opportunity to fulfill my dream of becoming an AUB student. My mother's basic salary as a teacher is 3,805,000 LL, and, like the other teachers, she receives $950 monthly in financial support from Saint Joseph School, Cornet Chehwan's Support Fund which includes parents' contributions and extra funding from outside the school. In addition to that, she receievs $827.78 annually to cover transportation fees to and from school. However, the difficulties are numerous, and I am counting on your empathy and good judgment to hope for financial assistance. Here is a breakdown of our monthly expenses: Generator: between $80 in summer and $150 in winter, as we cannot afford solar panels. Car maintenance and fuel: $100 to $120. Internet (Ogero) and landline: $20. Groceries: $300. Mobile phone recharge (for my mother and me): $15. Drinking water gallons: $30. Assistance for my grandparents: $100. Annually, my mother also has to pay: House water: $130. Car insurance: $80. Municipality fees: $60. N.B: My mother had a savings account with "SNA" since she was single. Due to the 2019 crisis, she tried to withdraw the funds, but it was impossible. The amount is held at Bank of Beirut, and I am sending the details in an attachment. She is allowed to withdraw $150 per month from the account. My mother has told me that AUB exceeds her financial limits, but I hope to count on your understanding to help me realize my dream of being a student at AUB. I am determined to keep my GPA above 3.5. With my Early Admission (30% discount), allocated to me because of my SAT score (1460) and my school grades (averages of 17.59 and 17.76, ranked 2nd and 3rd in 1S and 2S), I hope to receive an additional 50% reduction from you. Please grant this request, as without a 50% Financial Aid in addition to the 30% discount, I will be forced to consider another option that I believe is not right for me. I am aware of AUB's ranking and importance in the world, and I hope I will be able to attend it. Attached, you will find all the necessary documents to understand my situation. I am also ready to provide any additional information you may need. Thank you in advance for taking the time to read my message. Sincerely, Jessica Matta

parsed_special_family_circumstances_deta: 6 years ago, my parents invested their savings in the construction field aiming to benefit from selling after the building phase is done. Buyers paid down payments by check and continued paying the unsettled amount by checks. The bank is not paying my parents the equivalent amount of money by cash. Instead, it is paying 10 to 15 times less than the amount that should be paid. My parents are obliged to pay the construction material and construction employees by cash on the market rate of the currency ratio USD/LBP. Committed by contracts and not protected by the Lebanese laws my parents find themselves obliged to use all their savings. In two words, buyers of the apartments were paying by checks and my parents were obliged to pay the construction bills by fresh cash dollar to a point they became in debt and consumed all their savings. (Equivalent to bankruptcy) The law didn't protect my parents: by law, they are obliged to give away the apartments they worked to build during four years without getting anything in return other than a piece of paper (bank checks)that are not cashable and worth 15 times less than the amount written on it. My parents who are now in debt to the construction workers are trying to work hard at their dental clinic to pay all the bills related to construction in fresh cash dollars. The few apartments that are not sold remain unfinished due to lack of money. In their condition they cannot be rented or sold especially during the economic crisis the country is passing through Covid 19 pandemic didn't help at all, the clinics were almost closed for the past 5 years due to Covid 19. In addition, the economic crisis in Lebanon did not help: for the past 5 years, patients couldn't afford to treat their teeth. Without any fixed salary or income both my parents (dentists) found themselves in a catastrophic situation. NB: A property in my father's name in bhamdeun is not his property, but is my grandparents' house who are still living. So, my father cannot profit from this property personally. Concerning my mom's properties, she doesn't own any, but only a fraction of the shares that are divided between relatives who inherited. That is why she cannot profit from any income related to the properties. As for myself l am persevering in my studies and obtaining the best of grades in order to deserve the help l am asking for. The war situation for the past year made our financial situation even more difficult. Counting on you to assist me and give me the chance to excel in AUB.

parsed_special_family_circumstances_deta: I have been helping family and my siblings supporting expenses and tuition (high school and university) since the first paycheck I received as a part time tutor while I was going to high school. My family’s been heavily burdened and been facing significant financial challenges due to expensive medical treatment related to a case of illness that has been ongoing for the past few years. My brother’s treatment for acute mental illness and manic disorders involving doctor visits, hospitalizations, and 24-hour nursing supervision often, is very costly and mostly uninsured and uninsurable in Lebanon. Lack of constant and extensive treatment and follow up might lead to heart and cardiovascular conditions and possibly might lead to death. With the right treatment, management and support, most people with his disorder can live productive and fulfilling lives. My commitment to helping him achieve that, along with that of my parents’ have been the priority for us all. My father has sold and used each and every possible asset he’s earned and/or inherited to cover expenses related to my brother’s treatment. Nothing else left in his name, like the remaining inheritance, is of any value, either because of the non-cooperative inheritors/partners or because of location and cannot be sold or of any financial merit. Financial aid is imperative if I am to make my dreams a reality, and I am reaching out to you with a heartfelt plea for assistance. I believe that by investing in my education, you will not only be helping me achieve my goals but also supporting a family that is in need of a helping hand during this difficult time. I commit to work hard, excel in my studies, and make the most of this opportunity if given the chance, same as I did when I graduated in Industrial Engineering on a merit scholarship. I will be another one of the proud voices representing the institution that has helped so many students from Lebanon and the rest of the Arab world excel and go on to realize great achievements. Your support would mean the world to me and my family, and I am grateful for your consideration. I would like to express my gratitude in the future by giving back to honor those who helped me and to support future graduates on their journeys.

parsed_special_family_circumstances_deta: I am Maya Zaidan and I am currently a senior at the International School Of Choueifat. My mother, sister, and I live with my grandfather and his wife in his house in Mount Lebanon. My father is in UAE working and we haven't seen him for almost five years. My father has had health issues and has undergone surgeries and he currently is on medication. We do not have good communication with him since he is vague about his financial situation and he does not ask us about how our lives are here in Lebanon. However, from what we know, he is currently playing off a loan to the bank and is in debt to many people. I do not have all the details about the loan since he does not provide us with the accurate information. However, I have a document that I will upload. His monthly salary is 5,000 dirhams, where part of it goes to the bank to pay off the loan, part to pay off some of his debt, and part to buy himself medicine and necessities.So, he is only able to send us 500-1000$ each month. This amount has put us in a ton of pressure since we are barely able to get through the month. My mother is unemployed and is also in debt. With our monthly income from our father, we pay off some debt and are left with a small amount to be able to buy food and some necessities. In the moment, we are under pressure since we have my sister's university tuition and my senior year tuition. My sister is currently a second year student at aub and when she was still in school there was a discount on my tuition. However, now that she is in university, my tuition has had no discount on it since last year. We are struggling a lot to make ends meet and I want to be able to get educated at aub since my only hope is my education to be able to achieve my dreams. Because of our financial situation and the pressure it has put us in, my family and I are in constant stress and anxiety to what the future holds. We do not own any property or land or car nor do we have any bank savings to be able to help us with our financial situation. In addition, my mother, sister, and I live in my grandfather's house since we do not own our own house. We do not live on our own since we are unable to pay rent and our living situation is not very pleasant and that has also put us under stress. Right now, I am looking forward to completing my education and achieving my goals and making my life better for me and my family. Between having to pay off my sister and I's tuition, our debts, and some necessities, the money we are receiving each month is barely allowing us to afford the bare minimum. We have a ton of pressure on us right now since we are desperately trying to pay off my sister and I's tuition to be able to finish our education. I will be forever grateful if you are able to help me with my tuition to complete my education.

My mother is unable to legally work due to the Permanent Residence agreement by law in Lebanon, which adds significant financial strain. Her inability to contribute to the household income makes it even harder for us. Additionally, my mother’s inability to communicate in Arabic complicates her efforts to find support or resources that could assist us during this challenging time. As a result, our family is burdened with increased costs for medical care, daily living expenses, and transportation needs associated with my father’s condition. parsed_special_family_circumstances_deta: Following the financial crisis that affected all depositors in Lebanon, my parents lost a large portion of their essential savings (around $241,000; this account is frozen and its value is unfortunately in LOLLAR). Today, although my father is a lawyer, his work has significantly declined over the past two years due to the ongoing war, the institutional crisis, and frequent administrative shutdowns. It remains very difficult for him to recover financially. We depend almost entirely on my mother’s salary, who is a full-time teacher at Athénée de Beyrouth. In addition, my 86-year-old paternal grandmother is under my parents’ care, especially after the death of my grandfather in September 2024. She requires regular cardiac monitoring as she has seven stents, and she also needs constant personal assistance since she cannot live alone due to the rapid progression of Alzheimer’s disease. For me, receiving financial aid is essential; otherwise, I would not be able to enroll at AUB, especially since my parents will also have to pay my brother’s tuition, who will be in his final year of medical school. parsed_special_family_circumstances_deta: In 2016, my mother lost her job, before which she had been helping in covering our family expenses and after which this responsibility was left to my father entirely. While the Lebanese people have collectively experienced the economic hyperinflation repercussions since October 2019, my father has endured an additional difficulty in his work in the printing industry. Five years ago, he suffered great losses in his machinery and stock due to a flood, with no support to recover from the insurance. Meanwhile, his company Sprint Press needed to pay for the loan agreement which ended in 2022 and the company struggled to do so because of the hindrance in production due to the machinery loss. This was followed by the COVID-19 lockdown which resulted in the complete closure of the company for 2 years. Amidst this hardship occurred the Beirut blast, which caused much damage to the office, doors, electricity, and the computer alongside all its data. This resulted in a further regression in the production rates to less than 15-20% leaving the company’s bank accounts almost empty. While there were 7 employees in the company before, they all left due to the problematic financial situation, and my father became the sole employee left in his business, struggling to navigate these challenges on his own. During the end of 2023, my father decided to cancel his life insurance that he signed up for in 1998 so that he can obtain fresh money to cover some of our expenses. We have also been receiving monetary support from family members to the best of their ability given their own financial restraints. Additionally, the current war has led to a tremendous decline in my father’s work opportunities. My sister Celine has an almost full coverage of her tuition, in both her undergraduate and graduate years, through financial aid and donor funded scholarships which serve as the main factor in allowing her to pursue her studies and achieve her dreams. Note: Photos of the flood destruction, explosion damage, and loan agreement and payment documents are available upon request.

parsed_special_family_circumstances_deta: Dear Financial Aid Office, I hope this letter finds you well. My name is Mark, and I am applying for financial aid to support my dream of studying at the American University of Beirut (AUB). Allow me to share my story and circumstances, which I hope will help you understand how deeply I value this opportunity and why your support is essential. I was born at AUH in Beirut, a city I hold dear to my heart. Ever since I was a child, every visit to Beirut included a stop at AUB. Walking through its beautiful campus, imagining myself sitting in its classrooms, playing on its fields, and one day making my mark for AUB filled me with hope and determination. My connection to AUB is not only personal but generational-my mother was also born at AUH and grew up on campus, raised by my grandfather, an AUB graduate and a dedicated employee of the university for over 40 years. My aunts and uncles are proud AUB alumni as well. This legacy has inspired me to dream of one day taking AUB's name to great heights, joining the ranks of its alumni who have made a difference worldwide, shaped by the resilience and culture of this incredible institution. However, recent years have brought immense challenges to my family. The financial collapse in Lebanon wiped out the small savings my parents had managed to keep in the country. The COVID-19 pandemic further compounded our struggles-my father lost his job, and our situation in Dubai became unstable, forcing him to move to the United States in search of work, leaving us behind. This separation has had significant implications for our family. While he continues to work tirelessly, our financial situation remains difficult and unstable. While my father is focused on rebuilding his life, he is unable to provide financial support for my education at AUB or my stay in Lebanon. My dream of studying at AUB now feels out of reach due to these financial hurdles. I do not want to relocate to the United States-a place I visited only briefly as a baby and where I do not feel a sense of belonging. My heart and aspirations are tied to Beirut, to AUB, and to the future I hope to build there. I am determined to do whatever it takes to contribute to my education, including taking on student work. However, I cannot begin this journey without the financial support and funding that AUB can provide. I humbly ask for your understanding and assistance in making my dream a reality. Thank you for considering my application. I deeply appreciate your time and support, and I am hopeful that my story resonates with the spirit of generosity and resilience that AUB embodies. Sincerely, Mark

parsed_special_family_circumstances_deta: Before 2020, I never imagined my family's and my life would take such a turn and be defined by sickness, stress, and fear. My father had suffered from chronic health problems for years, but the economic crisis pushed him over the edge. He needs constant medical follow-up and six different medications to stay stable. The loss of his bank savings forced him to rely on loans repetitively. We have watched him grow weaker, struggling silently so we won’t worry, even though we see the pain in his face every day. On many occasions, his medications wouldn't even be available, and the fear of not finding them in time has become part of our daily life. My grandmother, who lives with us, has also seen her health collapse in these years. With no government support, she depends on us especially now that she suffers from Alzheimer. My mother, a public-sector worker, carries the weight of both of them on her shoulders. Her salary has collapsed due to the crisis and barely covers the basics, yet she keeps pushing herself because she has no other choice. My father’s engineering work and income have nearly disappeared especially given his deteriorating health. Most days, it feels like our house revolves around managing illnesses, running after pharmacies, trying to keep everyone stable. Watching the people I love fight their bodies-and the crisis-has been heartbreaking. Amid all this, my parents still try to protect my education, believing it’s the only light we have left. I work as a private tutor to help. My dream is to study at the American University of Beirut, just like my mother once did. I know the costs are far beyond our reach now, but with scholarship support, I hope I can do my studies, graduate, and finally be able to help my family heal-financially and emotionally-after everything they have endured.

parsed_special_family_circumstances_deta: Nada, my mother, experienced serious complications following the normal delivery of her second child. Shortly thereafter, she developed a pulmonary embolism in her lungs, which required multiple hospitalizations. As a result, she lost one lung and has since been placed on lifelong blood thinner medication to reduce the risk of additional clots. Despite this treatment, she later developed a clot near her spinal cord, which caused paralysis. Following hospital care and intensive rehabilitation, she was able to regain the ability to walk and perform basic daily activities, though she continues to rely on strong pain medication to manage her condition. Sometime later, she suffered another clot near her neck. While on her way to the hospital, the Beirut port explosion occurred, leading to a sudden increase in intracranial pressure. This caused severe and permanent damage to her vision and internal organs, ultimately leaving her partially blind. Since then, she has required continuous treatment to manage intracranial pressure and to preserve what remains of her partial vision. In addition to her medical struggles, our family faced severe financial hardship. Due to the Lebanese economic crisis, we were unable to secure insurance coverage for her treatments. At the same time, my father lost his job, which left us with no financial support. As a result, we had to use all our family savings and liquidate our assets to cover the high costs of her ongoing medical care. More recently, my father relocated to Denmark for work, while my mother, my sibling, and I continue to live in Lebanon. This situation has created the added burden of maintaining two households, with housing costs, basic utilities, and daily expenses in both countries. This dual financial responsibility alongside my mother’s ongoing medical needs has placed extraordinary pressure on our limited financial resources.

At this point, he had skin severe toxicity and the target therapy was exchanged to another type, that was not effective and new lesions started to grow again in his liver in spring 2024; he was put back to the initial chemo folfiri and target vectibix therapy that he is still taking continuously till other options could be found. Not only my father condition reduced the family income to less than half but also exhausted most of my parents cash savings , having to use them to compensate for the decrease in income and often to buy the very expensive target therapy when it is not available through the moh. All this adds to the Inability of my parents to use the bank account savings as, similar to all Lebanese, they are blocked since 2019.

As a result, my mother had to leave her job to take care of her, eliminating one of our household’s main sources of income. My father is now the sole provider, responsible for all family expenses as well as my grandmother’s needs, including food, medications, personal care items, and frequent medical and dental visits. Her separate health insurance costs about $5,000 per year, and many tests, treatments, and medications are not covered, leading to substantial out-of-pocket medical expenses. It is also important to clarify that my father’s reported income does not reflect his actual earnings. He is an insurance broker with no fixed salary; his income depends entirely on commissions that fluctuate each month. The reported gross income includes commissions he pays to third parties whose portfolios he manages and discounts he personally covers to complete sales. For instance, when offering clients reduced policy prices, the discounts are deducted from his commission but still counted as income. This practice reduces his real earnings by about 25%. Although his 2024 gross income was approximately $62,000, his actual net income was less than $47,000. Additionally, Lebanon’s ongoing economic crisis has severely affected our financial stability. The collapse of the banking sector and hyperinflation caused my father’s lifelong savings to lose over 90% of their value. The remaining amount is largely inaccessible due to strict withdrawal limits of less than $400 per month. The savings that were meant for emergencies and my education are effectively gone. Given these circumstances, receiving financial aid is essential to help reduce the financial burden of my education and allow me to pursue my studies at AUB.

parsed_special_family_circumstances_deta: We left our war-torn country in 2012, losing everything we had managed to build despite debilitating health issues in our family. My mother was diagnosed with Guillain Barre Syndrome in 1998. To afford the four sessions of plasmapheresis needed to save her, my parents paid every penny they had saved. Then, in 2002, my father started suffering from cardiac problems. The multiple catheterizations and the open heart surgery significantly set back our financial situation. Following his disk surgery in 2003, my father lost his ability to provide for his family. Just as we began to recover, the war in Syria broke out. Not only did we lose our savings, but we lost our home. With the little we had, we found refuge in Lebanon. Starting from zero, we faced unemployment and struggled with feelings of loss. This new beginning was already costly enough, but in 2013, I was diagnosed with severe scoliosis. My surgery cost more than 20,000 USD. Thankfully, I dealt with the reality of my lost dreams by holding onto academia. My community at school gathered the sum for my surgery by selling bracelets with "I Got Your Back" written on them. To this day, we struggle with our health. My father had urinary problems in 2022, underwent inguinal hernia surgery in 2023, and currently suffers from age-related health issues. My mother and I still face complications from the syndromes we overcame. Please find the relevant medical papers uploaded under additional documents. Despite it all, amidst these problems, my sense of community, admiration for medicine, and passion for its advancement have flourished. Hence, "that they may have life and have it more abundantly" holds a special place in my heart.
